newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal to sell near 30 percent of EDP.
newsitem.headline: Portugal to sell near 30 percent of EDP.

text.p: The Portuguese government plans to sell close to 30 percent of state-owned electricity concern EDP at its coming partial privatisation, including the portion set aside for the so-called green shoe, Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco said on Thursday.
He said 39 percent of the shares on offer would be sold directly to institutional investors, with the remainder going to the general public, employees and emigrants.
A proposed sale amounts to 29.9 percent of EDP's 600 billion escudo capital, or 179.96 million shares.

The public offer to sell (OPV) via the bourse, and including a special offer to small investors and employees, totals 99.79 million shares. The portion being sold directly to institutional investors totals 63.81 million shares, the minister said.
The breakdown of the OPV is as follows: 37.4 million shares to the general public; 5.93 million reserved for EDP employees and 56.2 million to small shareholders.

A senior ministry official said that in the case of the green shoe being fully exercised, the split between the domestic and international market would be 62.5 percent for the former and 37.5 percent for the latter.
